correctness.rationale: All five invariant-factor types and all 1,820 unordered row sets and 1,820 unordered column sets are accounted for. Exact cyclotomic determinant-coefficient testing in Z[z]/(z^8+1) and an independent 97-adic-image rank test agree for every counted aggregate, and a third unreduced enumeration verifies orbit weighting. Every determinant coefficient has absolute value at most 4! = 24; 97 is therefore large enough for the eight-root test to be equivalent to complex nonvanishing. The classification is finite and exhaustive, not extrapolated.

value.rationale: Determining exactly when a four-frequency signal is recoverable from four samples is a natural finite Fourier interpolation problem. The complete five-group census isolates a substantial dependence of sampling degeneracy on group structure at fixed cardinality and shows that the fourth-order rank-four count alone distinguishes all five isomorphism types. This supplies a complete natural small-order classification, rather than an arbitrary slice or an instance of merely changing a parameter.
